headline: Trump addressed what he knew about Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy as calls grew for Huang to resign, while CSET mapped the US-China AGI race and METR's report pointed toward AI self-improvement by 2027.

points.text: President Trump addressed what he knew about Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, as Transformer argued Huang should resign for misleading investors and Axios reported Nvidia has no clear succession plan.

CSET examined two distinct paths the US and China are taking toward artificial general intelligence, with the US leading in frontier models and compute while China pursues robotics, embodiment, and brain-inspired systems.
IEEE Spectrum detailed efforts to build a 'Find My'-style tracking system for AI chips, after years of export-restricted US chips turning up in China anyway.
In a 60 Minutes interview, Trump said AI safety risks are manageable and not as real as AI executives claim.
An extensive METR report found AI R&D acceleration at Anthropic is pushing toward potential recursive self-improvement by 2027.
OpenAI launched 'Control Room,' a central system to track and rapidly stop model workloads across its research infrastructure if safety or security concerns arise.
